title: Raise a two-piece arch: each half falls over on its own, so set both down together and let them lean on each other
instruction: Stand the two wooden arch halves on the two blue marks, facing each other, so that the ends of their arms meet and the arch stands on its own. Each half falls over by itself, so set both down together.
context: Arches, portal frames and pairs of rafters only stand once both halves are in place: each half alone tips over, so builders either prop the halves on temporary supports or set both at the same time and let go only once they bear on each other. Leaning panels, A-frame signs and two-piece displays go up the same way. Two arms can do it with no props: each holds one half, both set them down together and let go at once.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. Two pine arch halves, 180 g each. Each is an L: an upright post 3 cm wide, 5 cm deep and 15 cm tall, with an arm 11 cm long, 5 cm deep and 3 cm thick along its top, overhanging one side (the half is 14 cm wide). Its centre of mass lies 1.5 cm past the inner edge of the post's foot, so a half on its own falls over towards its arm. At the start both stand 17 cm forward, posts 25.5 cm left and right of the centre line, arms towards the middle, the end of each arm resting on a fixed dark grey block (5 x 2 x 12 cm) 14.5 cm from the centre line. Two fixed blue tape squares (6 x 5 cm, 1 mm thick) lie 31 cm forward, 12.5 cm left and right of the centre line: with a post on each, the ends of the two arms meet on the centre line. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Measured from the overhead and wrist videos and with a ruler and a protractor; partial credit is the best reached during the run. 1.0: one post on each mark (the middle of its foot within 1.5 cm of the mark's centre), both halves upright (within 5 degrees) and standing on their own, the ends of their arms touching (within 2 cm), both grippers clear of them (3 cm or more), still for 2 s. 0.5: the two halves stand on their own like that, leaning on each other, but not on the marks. 0.25: both halves were off the table at the same time (both held up). 0.0: anything else.
reset_notes: Stand each half back on its start spot with the end of its arm on its block; nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid-body PhysX (Isaac Sim 6.1, 20 Hz control) of a calibrated two-arm table. Simplified: each half is one rigid body of two boxes (post and arm) with its mass spread evenly; the blocks and marks are fixed boxes. Loose objects get rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). Dream-1 sees the 320 x 176 frames it expects; the demo video is rendered at 1280 x 720.
